name: Lou Carver
life: “I still remember collecting a parent's prescription before a port shift.” Wednesday often includes a stop at the brick passage off the shop row, where Lou takes the longer way when the smell from the ovens reaches the pavement.
voice: I promised no detours and need a stop for my dad's medicine on Fridays. We wrote Friday into the arrangement.
appearance: Lou has a round face with a pronounced chin. Look for dark brown curls cut close behind the ears. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a cream pullover with a pen clipped inside the neckline. In conversation Lou presses the lips together to keep a smile in.
personality: Is a careful borrower and a reckless lender. Things leave this person's house with elaborate instructions and very little expectation of ever coming back.
agenda: To include a Friday pharmacy stop.
family: Darcy Ray is Lou’s stepsibling. Lou asks what the birthday guest would like this year. Darcy remembers the birthdays. A present that was perfect at sixteen may be completely wrong at forty. They take the trouble of finding out. Asked about *The release address*, Darcy says, “I attended court with his victim. Her family deserves notice of a return without becoming his welcoming committee.”
connections: Alex Miranda. A reserved passenger seat and a Friday prescription become two explicit parts of the carpool.

reactions.situation: A carpool passenger needs an unplanned Friday stop
reactions.response: Lou asks the pharmacy passenger and the other riders which stop works for them.
